steps.title: Card testing
steps.say: Start with the burst. Tiny amounts, many merchants, a device the customer has never used, then a gift card that actually clears. The suggestion is block. Do not press it yourself.
steps.summary: Card testing on Colin Ellis: tiny probes, then $186.00 on a new device.

steps.title: Account takeover
steps.say: Contrast this with the trip you will open last. Here the device is new, the country is new, and the spend is gift cards and crypto at many times the baseline.
steps.summary: Account takeover on Anika Nguyen: new device, new country, spend at 56.1× baseline.

steps.title: Mule-account chain
steps.say: Follow the money, not the single payment. Shared devices, a young account, and a path that ends at a crypto cash-out the same day.
steps.summary: Mule flow touching Idris Bennett: funds move onward to a cash-out the same day.

steps.title: Merchant collusion
steps.say: The fourth pattern. Round amounts, one merchant, buyers who share a laptop. Escalating one card does not fix the merchant.
steps.summary: Collusive buying at Northwind Digital Keys, including Colin Costa.

steps.title: Genuine customer
steps.say: This one was queued. Halden reads the file and approves it. This is the false alarm the rubber-stamp desk would have blocked.
steps.summary: Marcus Costa is travelling on a device already on file. The foreign IP is the trip, not a takeover.
